marker codes. The marker code is interpreted as required, and the buffer pointer remains pointed to the 0xFF prefix of

findings.rationale: The matching branch adds 0xff00, sets bit_count to eight and caches a marker at the unchanged prefix offset without changing byte_position or current_byte. result.notes:
Standalone, source-only partial publication pass. No inference, tests, proofs, builds or legacy pipeline were run. Assignment has 51 Core specs across 27 arithmetic components. Full contracts were requested/read with read_specs for ArithmeticContext::new, ArithmeticDecoder::new, decode_integer, decode_iaid and byte_in_signal (14 assigned specs total); the subject-wide read_specs returned no specs, so exact component subjects were used. All 14 received forward retrieval calls; transient MCP failures/unknown-work-item responses in parallel calls were retried serially successfully. Retrieval uses local SOMA 0.4.0/Potion with budgeted selection, not a relevance cutoff. Forward constructor retrieval was paginated at offset 5; reverse A.3 retrieval was paginated at offset 3 and eventually returned bc8b68efc88af33fe2e83615 even though its first page did not. Reverse BYTEIN retrieval returned the refill wrapper specs and 076993dab5b42889539bdf3e. Full-text enumeration reports 392 passages; lexical enumeration reports 421 obligation candidates. Sampled passage pages at offsets 0, 300 and 340 and obligation pages at 0 and 300; neither enumeration is claimed exhaustive. search_rfc covered arithmetic integer, initialization, resetting statistics and SBSYMCODELEN, and read_rfc_section supplied A, A.2, A.3, E, E.3.4, E.3.5, E.3.7 and 6.4.2. E.3.1-.3 were also exposed by full-text passage enumeration. All submitted IDs came from host retrieval/search/enumeration, not invented anchors.
Reusable survey: config/support-matrix.json names ITU-T T.88 (08/2018), ISO/IEC 14492:2019 Edition 2 and a project-defined broad bi-level decoder profile, explicitly not full Annex F profile 1 conformance. README excludes encoding and warns that implemented features are not full JBIG2 conformance. The assigned T.6 source is the 1988-amended edition (file t6-198811.txt; hash ce107ab4f36fb3b7a1f17f2e076472370144973b0e0e2202183ca994735d17e8). T.88 is t88-201808.txt, hash 0caacf3891e7b059ef8090ec96029768b2621aa366ce4b37a3a56f743ec475c6, bearing ITU 08/2018 and ISO/IEC 14492:2019 labels. No newer-edition conformance is inferred. Annexes A and E explicitly form integral parts of the standard. Annex E says flowcharts/tables define outputs that alternative implementations shall duplicate: representation choices and physical context sizes are not automatically deviations. MUST/SHOULD/MAY labels are lexical annotations; the sampled T.6 copyright MAY is not a decoder requirement.
Source trace: arithmetic.rs documents Annex E rather than the non-normative Annex G complemented-register convention. decode_integer calls integer-bit and integer-bits helpers; decode_iaid calls decode; decode dispatches through decode_signal/lower/upper and renormalize_signal to byte_in_signal. All these nearby production bodies were read, but this pass does not replace their uninvestigated stored contracts. ArithmeticCodec chooses procedure banks via field.slot(), stores separate integer banks and an independent IAID vector, and forwards symbol-ID widths. Generic sessions prevalidate bounded terminators and later validate observed markers. generic_region/segments.rs also has a known-length trailing-FF adaptation path, so strict low-level EOF must not be confused with rejection of every stream lacking an explicit final marker. Full treatment of that adaptation was not audited. E.3.4's non-consuming marker fill is directly supported by the readable prose and source branch, not merely by an existing Core summary.
No external-standard finding was fabricated for the six other explored contracts: constructor acceptance/error formatting (4122feb02283157b9dac28c8), integer partial-error state (155573487250f03cb70f5e41), IAID frame/preflight validation (bde58d905d2f68b156b25987, d5f87a3f8d4995afac006102), or refill EOF/overflow mutation order (1db5ad401fd5e2cacb5e9188, ac84fedf1e465eda9d866f2f). These express useful local API behavior, but the inspected standard passages do not settle identical error-state requirements.
Unrelated candidates retained only as survey notes: T.88 6.2.6/T.6 MMR rules concern the separate MMR branch, not the assigned arithmetic endpoint; sampled Annex B Huffman table construction/decoding and 8.2 page-buffer/striping rules concern other components. Encoder-only production obligations do not apply to this decoder role. E.2.10 is useful decoder fill-bit context despite its encoder-oriented heading, not an automatic missing-encoder defect. All implemented labels refer only to the narrow quoted clause and stated domain. Source quotations were manually inspected and are not host-verified function attributions or semantic proofs.

document_quote.quote:
OR              If V1 and V2 are two binary values, then V1 OR V2 is equal to 0 if both V1 and V2 are 0. It is equal to
                1 if either of V1 or V2 is 1. If V1 and V2 are two integer values, then it is the result of bitwise
                application of OR.
AND             If V1 and V2 are two binary values, then V1 AND V2 is equal to 0 if either of V1 or V2 is 0. It is equal
                to 1 if both V1 and V2 are 1. If V1 and V2 are two integer values, then it is the result of bitwise
                application of AND.
XOR             If V1 and V2 are two binary values, then V1 XOR V2 is equal to 0 if V1 and V2 are equal. It is equal to
                1 if V1 and V2 differ. If V1 and V2 are two integer values, then it is the result of bitwise application of
                XOR.
XNOR            If V1 and V2 are two binary values, then V1 XNOR V2 is equal to 0 if V1 and V2 differ. It is equal to 1
                if V1 and V2 are equal.
REPLACE         If V1 and V2 are two binary values, then V1 REPLACE V2 is equal to V2.

findings.rationale: The scalar match implements the five Boolean definitions directly. The u8 and u64 matches perform the same operation independently on each stored pixel bit, including XNOR via complemented XOR and REPLACE via the source operand. compose_chunked and the region kernels actually call the byte/word variants. This finding covers operator meaning, not parsing numeric operator fields, deciding which operator a segment is allowed to use, or all page-composition rules. Source comparison is not a semantic proof.
findings.relevance: T.88 (08/2018) 4.3 defines the operators used by this decoder's bitmap-composition primitives. Destination corresponds to V1 and source to V2, which is essential for REPLACE. This is a normative definition without a modal-word prerequisite, not a network endpoint requirement.

document_quote.quote:
A pixel in a bitmap is referred to by a pair of coordinates X and Y, sometimes written as a pair (X, Y). The location
(0, 0) represents the pixel in the top left corner. The X coordinate increases rightwards and the Y coordinate increases
downwards.

findings.rationale: Both access paths address row y at y*stride and byte floor(x/8); pixel_mask selects the corresponding MSB-first bit. Increasing x moves through pixels within a row and increasing y moves to the next row. Checked bounds exclude logical row padding. MSB-first packing and None/IntegerOverflow for invalid accesses are local API choices, not requirements inferred from 5.6. In particular, Note 1's usual black/white interpretation is explicitly not a universal T.88 requirement.
findings.relevance: The decoder's in-memory bitmap accessor and updater realize the logical coordinate convention used throughout T.88. Applicability assumes a canonical row-major bitmap with stride ceil(width/8) and accessible storage. The standard defines logical coordinates here, not a mandatory byte packing or physical orientation.

assumptions: Rust references and borrowing are valid; canonical storage is a premise for the logical pixel interpretation, not a safety precondition on the public getter.

evidence.quote: /// Returns a pixel, or `None` when the coordinates are outside the bitmap.

spec.nl: For canonical accessible bitmap storage and an in-bounds coordinate, return the Boolean value of the row-major pixel selected by bit 7-(x mod 8); coordinates outside the logical bitmap return None. Reading leaves storage unchanged, and set_pixel updates the corresponding selected bit.

Reusable implementation facts: shared collection preserves dictionary/export order and has contiguous/borrowed representations; dictionary and text dispatch both consume that codebook; refinement dispatch uses complete RegionInfo equality, page snapshots and a fresh refinement-statistics wrapper; pattern and halftone arithmetic wrappers share GenericArithmeticSession initialization. T.88 D.3 permits embedding-format-specific segment placement: its flexible storage organization is not by itself a requirement that these contiguous-stream APIs parse PDF containers or arbitrary interleaved container bytes. No out-of-scope finding was created. Seed 036c0448b7ae64feda507c27's reusable-scratch cleanup and seed 273ee83cf0d35be6a8658bc5's work/memory accounting are project API/resource contracts, with no identified external requirement for these exact counters or vector lengths. Seed 1054b4700d411cc3108f7760 describes eligibility for an optimization; 8.2 permits output-equivalent strategies, but eligibility alone does not establish full direct-path raster equivalence, so no equivalence finding was manufactured. Evidence is confined to the assigned text conversions and current source observations. The release helper only removes resources for explicit Some(false), preserving true/missing flags and unrelated entries, then debits packed bitmap bytes. Separately, document/references.rs validates that a false referred flag occurs at the last referring segment, and rejects later references. This supports release timing for validated local segments. Standalone source/document publication pass. Read get_work_item, rfc_inventory, and the complete read_specs results for all ten assigned components/all sixteen assigned Core specs, retaining their stated assumptions and intent labels. No previous attempt feedback was present. Initial concurrent candidate requests intermittently returned tool errors or 'unknown work item'; sequential retries obtained candidates for every assigned spec. All 392 full-text passages and 421 lexical obligations were enumerated using consecutive pagination, and their component-related resource/retention concepts surveyed; enumeration is not full semantic adjudication. Forward retrieval was paginated for f375180ca9a3ed6ca8bd800a and reverse retrieval of retention passage a340f811881d1c7688dc5fcc2f27600767ac294a5a29d22c287962a7d6351df6 was paginated through its ten budget-selected specs. Reverse retrieval of 7.1 was also inspected. SOMA results were treated only as local budgeted candidates, never a relevance threshold or an absence proof.

Read complete nearby T.88 sections 7.2.3, 7.2.4, 7.4.2.2, 8.1 and 8.2 and the informative 0.1.4 and 7.4.10 context. search_rfc queries were 'retention', 'memory', 'work', 'discard' and 'limit'. Exact passage IDs come from these tools and enumeration. Lexical annotations are not normative classification: for example 7.2.4's prohibition on later references is labelled MAY because it contains 'may', and the initial T.6 obligations include publication/legal prose and false lexical matches. Used the full 7.2.4 meaning and 7.1 discard permission, not an isolated modal label. The three stored findings intentionally cover only cleanup after current-segment consumption. They are separate resource classes, not three claims of whole 7.2.4 compliance.

Reusable source survey: resources.rs contains first-match lookups, insertion checks, RetainedBudget's checked add/subtract, retain_bitmap/release_bitmap, and all assigned helpers. retain_bitmap charges bitmap.bytes().len() and release_bitmap debits the same stored-byte unit; neither transfers bitmap ownership. bitmap_byte_len (58e95ff372b3097a83445919) counts packed backing length, not capacity; Bitmap::bytes returns &self.data, and allocated_bytes separately uses capacity. Retain specifications 7f7726f73761c6e7cb2f7d8f/88269394553da2090143f8cd and release specification c8322337cdbb63b8bd68f679 describe inclusive project budget and typed arithmetic/error policy, not requirements to allocate/free a particular number of bytes in T.88. allocation_size (d316eb9de3e67988eb720c52) computes checked count*size_of<T> requested inline storage without allocating. structural_work (80243d67f1637d3830a7b3d5), structural_work_totals (47d87341c479e7fcc4ee45d1) and checked_work_add (b575c23342218ca9b5b7c3bd) compute checked input bytes + segment count + reference count for local abstract work admission. Their exact arithmetic and error classes are project policy; no independent normative equation was established. src/limits.rs documents inclusive resource maxima; docs/spec-traceability.md expressly separates resource/error policy from normative rules. T.88 0.1.4 is informative and does not specify internal storage; 8.1/8.2 require equivalent final results rather than identical internal steps. Thus these arithmetic helpers were not spuriously mapped as normative omissions or deviations.

Pattern/symbol dispatch charges exported bitmap bytes before publishing resources. Both global and ordinary orchestration release resources after dispatch. Pattern and symbol removal precedes byte counting and scalar debit; their failure contracts e9c01d9d76a97d8e696240a1 and 45326fc82dd2306c590b1c11 describe partial mutation on accounting failure, not a normative rollback guarantee or detected standards defect. Removed SymbolResource owns both exported bitmaps and optional contexts; bitmap accounting does not claim to measure all context/capacity bytes. document/references.rs additionally rejects known later local references after a false retain flag, but this supportive read is not a complete global/reference-resolution audit. RetentionFlags::retain_referred_segment uses index+1 and conservatively returns None for absent positions.

Unrelated retrieval candidates retained here rather than submitted as out-of-scope findings: arithmetic encoder BYTEOUT (E.2.7), probability estimation (E.2.5), colour palette parameters (6.8.2), profile F graphic-arts constraints, Annex J encoder recommendations, Huffman selection (7.4.2.1.6), T.6 terminal negotiation/run coding, embedded ordering details (D.3), comment extension encodings (7.4.15.1), and Annex H worked examples do not impose the assigned scalar helper or cleanup contracts. BMSIZE/uncompressed row storage in 6.5.9 is not allocation_size<T> or the byte sum of separate pattern/symbol store entries. Informative annex/prose candidates were not promoted to decoder requirements merely because they contain MUST/SHOULD/MAY.

Detailed bidirectional candidate/source investigation in this bounded pass covered eleven assigned specs: 4742abbeceff67743781b06c, 5b601d13c1a688cc10f5fcbf, 7382b440cf627c79ee8b7f8e, 727513d7e963faea76ccc4ea, 381e99630ec95553acb229ea, 9e814169eb5322de19ffe01b, 74fd18abde12c90491cb5905, a9655b536df2010611fabe94, b61b5e9ea1e4c688cf9d2060, df89e94d1428ceefcb7a6a01 and 30b98406bd1436f126b08007. The fourteen findings intentionally map selected propositions, not all clauses in those eleven contracts.
Corpus is fulltext+obligations/1, not legacy lexical-only. Paginated rfc_passages enumerated all 392 passage records (offsets 0,5,205); paginated rfc_obligations enumerated all 421 lexical records (offsets 0,5,205). Enumeration is an inventory survey, not substantive analysis of every record. SOMA was used spec-first and in reverse, with an additional forward page for organization (offset 5) and reverse page for the first-page obligation (offset 1). Results were treated as budgeted candidates, never a relevance threshold. In particular reverse D.2 retrieved an embedded API and several page-association queries retrieved is_striped: these are unrelated candidate associations, not defects or missing implementation. Search_rfc for resolution, page height, striping, end row, embedded organization, number of pages, page association and referred-to segment numbers recovered exact full-text passage IDs outside the first shortlist.
Original sections read with read_rfc_section included T.88 Annex D, D.1, D.2, D.3, D.4.2, D.4.3, 7.2.5, 7.2.6, 7.4.8.2, 7.4.8.3, 7.4.8.4, 7.4.8.6, 7.4.9 and 7.4.10; candidate and enumeration text supplied nearby context including 7.1 and 8.2. Annex D expressly forms an integral part of the standard, so its definitions can govern implementation without uppercase modal words. Introductory 0.1.3, examples in H.1, encoder-organization advice in 11.3, publication copyright text, and unrelated coding algorithms were not converted into decoder defects merely because lexical or similarity retrieval returned them. The 7.2.5 lower-reference sentence crosses a PDF page break, and one lexical quote stops at 'lower'; the full section supplies its continuation. Field definitions and table bits were examined as potential normative content independently of modal extraction.
Source tracing read actual implementation and documentation in src/document.rs, src/document/input.rs, src/document/pages.rs, src/document/parsing.rs, src/document/references.rs, src/file_header.rs, src/segment_data.rs, src/reader.rs, src/segment_header.rs, src/decode/api.rs, src/decode/orchestration.rs and README.md. Public inspection only validates structural envelopes/page lifecycle, not compressed region pixels; successful inspection is not successful decoding. Reader APIs buffer bounded compressed input before inspection. DecoderContext wrappers forward the associated Decoder's result then call finish_call. Embedded APIs consume caller-extracted segment streams, do not parse PDF containers, and reuse Sequential as envelope metadata rather than asserting a nonexistent standalone organization flag. Globals deliberately restrict input to page-independent segments and are later supplied to decoding via their retained bytes; such an API restriction is not a defect in general JBIG2 page-associated syntax. Internal Vec lookup/ownership, reusable scratch capacity and quota policies do not acquire a standards obligation simply through topical similarity to decoder buffers.
Evidence is source quotation and existing-contract composition only. No inference stage, test, build, probe, proof, model checker or legacy pipeline was run, and no production code was changed. File quotations are not host-verified function attributions or semantic proofs. Stored alignment is not whole-component, whole-edition, Annex F profile, or decoded-pixel compliance.

findings.rationale: Read all of 7.4.14, including the distinction between necessary and dependent extensions and the necessary-implies-reserved restriction. parse_known_segment_data dispatches extension payloads to parse_extension; it reads the four-byte type and propagates classify_extension errors. classify_extension first validates flags, then returns Unsupported(Extension(original_type)) for bit 31. UnsupportedFeature::fmt retains the u32 identifier in its diagnostic and DecodeError::fmt adds the unsupported category. This implements the project's documented supported-profile boundary consistently with the standard's explanation of necessary data. The standard does not require this Rust error type, wording, hexadecimal padding, or abort strategy; those are project diagnostics, not additional normative requirements. This source comparison is not a semantic proof or whole-file conformance result.

RA2 is reference-plane and accepts all signed-byte offsets, unlike causal target RA1. Generic typical prediction copies complete rows and precedes skip logic; refinement typical prediction uses uniform 3x3 reference neighbourhoods per pixel. Blank-target assumptions are essential because both kernels generally write only true pixels. Allocating callers create blank bitmaps; direct-into and row-ring paths were not certified. Reusable facts: this is decoder-side arithmetic scratch storage, not a wire protocol endpoint. try_decode is selected for GenericContextDescriptor::NominalTemplate0; decode_generic_on additionally requires no skip bitmap. Both ordinary four-AT nominal coordinates and the nominal twelve-AT extended coordinates can produce that descriptor. Non-nominal adaptive coordinates and other templates use decode_generic_with rather than being rejected by the row-ring module. A declined optimization returns before any probability decision and the caller falls back. The ring keeps min(rows,3) physical rows, has ceil(width/32) u32 words per row, uses modulo slots, clears before reuse, and flushes complete byte rows. row_word reads stride bits, not an independently width-masked stream; zero-valued unused bits depend on the ring's actual initialization/writer discipline. The relational spec de99cbff8c94939562ea3c23 compares the ordinary nominal, no-skip fallback on initially zero requested bitmap rows; it does not establish equivalence for arbitrary prefilled into-destinations, errors, or all extended-template layouts.

No independent external-standard requirement was identified in the inspected sections for Rust ownership/drop, checked-index error identities, prefix-commit failure behavior, a three-slot allocation, or the exact charged-byte formula. Keep these as Core engineering contracts, not manufactured ITU requirements or absence findings. storage_bytes computes logical payload 4*ceil(width/32)*min(rows,3); fits_managed_memory adds supplied context/bitmap charges and uses an inclusive limit; try_new can decline independently (including its u32 width+31 check and reservation failure). charged_bytes is requested payload, not a measurement of vector capacity/allocator overhead. Limits and README document resource policy; the searched standard's memory mentions do not automatically prescribe that local policy.

limitations: This is partial stored alignment, not whole-component, whole-stream, profile or whole-standard compliance. Only the explicitly described aspect of each quoted passage is classified; repeated passage IDs do not assert all clauses in the passage.

The source is PDF-converted local text. Mathematical glyphs, tables, figure geometry and page/section boundaries may be imperfect; Figure 26 was not visually checked against the original PDF. No newer T.88/T.6 edition was acquired or assessed.

All assigned specs were read and seeded with candidate retrieval, but the corpus survey was bounded rather than exhaustive: remaining passage/obligation pages and much of T.88 4.2, 6.2, 6.7, 7.4.5.2, Annex F, Annex E and T.6 were not investigated to clause-complete coverage. Resource-policy specs listed in notes remain without a demonstrated normative counterpart, not demonstrated unrelated to every possible standard provision.

The one-pattern/HBPP=0 interpretation remains unresolved between 6.6.5 and Annex C.5. Zero grid/region dimensions and extreme dictionary counts were not settled as standard-valid input domains; helper arithmetic behavior must not be mistaken for their normative admissibility.

The retained outer rendering contract's conditional arithmetic-state normalization requirement, canonical-pattern condition and review-marked descriptor/table/helper assumptions remain in force. This pass did not independently verify entropy tables, generic/refinement decoding, every MMR/EOFB rule, arithmetic markers, all chunked bitmap paths, public caller obligations or compiler configurations.

Separate finalization and state progress were source-traced, but no normative retry/rollback/cleanup requirement was established for the assigned ownership/lifecycle clauses. result.notes:
Standalone source/document publication pass. Read get_work_item, rfc_inventory and the full read_specs contracts for all 13 assigned components/24 assigned spec IDs, including the lengthy rendering contract's conditional arithmetic normalization requirement and review-marked helper assumptions; labels were not treated as invalidating facts. Initial concurrent host reads/retrievals intermittently returned unknown-item/JSON/tool errors and one empty spec list; sequential retries supplied inventory, both missing contracts and candidates for every assigned spec. No inference, tests, builds, proofs, probes, resolve_obligation or legacy pipeline were run; no source files were edited.

Corpus is fulltext+obligations/1, not a lexical-only legacy corpus. Sources remain T.88 (08/2018) edition 2.0 (converted text also bears ISO/IEC 14492:2019(E) footers) and T.6 (1988 Blue Book extract); they do not establish conformity to an unspecified newer edition. SOMA forward retrieval was used for every assigned spec, including pagination for generate_skip_mask; reverse passage retrieval investigated HSKIP, rendering and Annex C, and reverse obligation retrieval investigated clipping. Supplemented with fulltext search HSKIP, HNUMPATS, memory (both pages), MMR flag constraints and Gray coding. Enumerated passage pages 0-3, 140-144 and 149-158 of 392 and obligation pages 0-14 and 120-146 of 421. Read complete indexed sections 6.1, 6.6.5, 6.6.5.1, 6.6.5.2, 7.4.5.1.1, C.5 and 8.1. No similarity threshold or empty result was used to establish absence; changed context budgets can change SOMA totals, so its pagination is not an exhaustive catalog. Exact IDs in findings are returned indexed IDs.

Source trace: read render.rs and resources.rs completely; followed planes.rs (gray depth, decode requests, XOR, row-major accumulation, shape validation), bitmap storage/region/operators, halftone header parser, GenericRegionState's real Arithmetic/GrayMmr branches and separate finish, WorkBudget declarations, Limits and dispatch call sites. Project docs/spec-traceability.md expressly separates resource/error policy from normative rules and disclaims complete standard conformance. Local ghost models/annotations are evidence of documented project intent, not independent standard authorities or proofs. Findings are file-quotation-supported source assessments; host quote matching is not a host-verified function attribution or semantic theorem.

Read supporting reader.rs byte/bit decoding, validation.rs including final endpoint checks, wide.rs arithmetic, and prefix-lookup construction. The four-limb representation supports long prefixes; the u16 cache declines unrepresentable row IDs rather than truncating them, retaining canonical fallback. Reviewed stored facts were used normally with their assumptions, not discarded for needs_review labels.

Important applicability resolution: B.2 step 5(d)'s CURRANGELOW >= HTHIGH initially looks broader than the parser's exact partition check. B.2.3 defines HTHIGH as one greater than the last normal upper bound, so the inspected exact-endpoint checks are not a demonstrated deviation. B.2 says OOB has no range, resolving B.4's generic read-suffix step for OOB. Section 6.1 leaves behavior on bitstream restriction violations undefined; ReservedFlags, EOF, oversubscription, error ordering, cursor behavior after failure and allocation diagnostics are project policy, not all externally required errors.

document_quote.quote: Read one bit at a time until the bit string read matches the code assigned to one of the table lines.

findings.rationale: The production fallback reads one bit per iteration and calls append_bit before testing for a matching canonical code. The helper delegates to checked_shift_left_one followed by checked_add_small; inspection of both bodies shows inter-limb carry propagation and explicit overflow rejection. BitReader reads each byte most-significant-bit first, consistent with nearby T.88 5.4.1, and accumulation shifts older prefix bits toward greater significance. Four u64 limbs accommodate the project's maximum 255-bit prefixes. The assigned contract's behavior for arbitrary u32 arguments and 256-bit storage overflow is broader than the standard-facing binary-bit use and is not itself a normative T.88 requirement. Project annotations/models document this local intent; they are not independent standard-fidelity proofs. Source quotations establish this scoped alignment, not host-verified function attribution, a semantic proof, cached-path equivalence, or full B.4 compliance.
findings.relevance: T.88 (08/2018), normative Annex B, B.4 step 1 applies to the Huffman decoder role, not an encoder or the arithmetic/MMR decoding paths. The assigned append_bit contract supplies the incremental bit-string representation used by decode_fallback. This finding covers accumulation of a binary prefix only, not the entirety of B.4. Applicability assumes a valid constructed Huffman table and reader; the production caller obtains each argument from read_bits(1), so bit is 0 or 1.

/// Decodes one integer or OOB value according to T.88 B.4.

spec.nl: When accumulating a Huffman prefix from successive binary input bits, append_bit is intended to shift the existing wide prefix left one position and append the new bit at the low-order position, propagating failure instead of silently wrapping.
spec.subject: src/huffman/wide.rs:76:huffman::wide::WideCode::append_bit

document_quote.quote:
Let I be the index of the table line whose code
              was decoded.

findings.rationale: Construction records per-length first_code, length_count, first_line, and ordered_lines; it scans source lines in increasing index order when filling each length bucket. decode_fallback passes the accumulated prefix, first_code[length], and length_count[length] to small_distance_from, then adds a successful distance to first_line[length] to obtain the original table-line index. The inspected range helper propagates all four subtraction borrows and rejects a final borrow, nonzero upper difference limbs, a non-u32 distance, and the exclusive count endpoint. The exact subtraction and half-open-range contracts already stored for the two assigned specs explain why a wrapped low limb must not create a false match; this pass does not rerun inference or prove those contracts. The project-authored model and annotations document this support relationship. B.3 supplies the canonical contiguous ordering needed by this mapping; without coherent construction metadata, the scalar helpers alone cannot establish line selection. Implemented denotes this local range-to-line-selection contribution only, not complete B.4 value decoding, all malformed-stream handling, or end-to-end conformance.
findings.relevance: B.4 step 1 requires selecting the line whose assigned code matches the input prefix. For canonical tables constructed according to B.3, codes of a fixed length form a consecutive interval in original table-line order. small_distance_from implements membership and the exact offset in that interval; subtract_limb is its four-stage arithmetic support. The decoder endpoint and a coherent table produced by from_line_source are assumed. T.88 does not require this limb representation, borrow algorithm, or a u32 offset API; subtract_limb is mapped transitively as implementation support, not as a separately prescribed standard algorithm.

evidence.quote: /// A validated table with canonical prefix codes assigned as in T.88 B.3.

spec.nl: During canonical Huffman prefix matching, small_distance_from is intended to return the exact nonnegative offset from the first assigned code only when that offset is below the number of codes at the current length; its limb-subtraction support must not allow a negative or wide difference to alias a valid table entry.
spec.subject: src/huffman/wide.rs:107:huffman::wide::WideCode::small_distance_from

document_quote.quote: assigns a unique prefix code to each table line, of the length given by PREFLEN for that table line.

findings.rationale: Construction computes the B.3 first-code recurrence with canonical_first_code and, for each nonempty bucket, checks canonical_range_fits before accepting its metadata. That helper computes the last assigned code as first + count - 1 and calls fits_in_bits(length). fits_in_bits rejects any higher nonzero limb and any bit at or above the requested cutoff; widths at least 256 accept all four-limb values, consistent with its stored broad mathematical contract. The production prefix domain is at most 255, documented by MAX_PREFIX_LEN and WideCode's comment; B.2.1 permits an HTPS of eight, which can encode prefix lengths through 255. This extra storage capacity is not a deviation. The annotation and project model document the width-check intent, and the caller converts failure to Oversubscribed. The standard excerpt supports required assigned width but does not independently mandate this exact invalid-table error policy or establish that every rejected malformed table must be rejected. No proof, build, or test was run, and whole-table canonical assignment is not certified.
findings.relevance: Normative B.3 governs canonical code assignment by the Huffman table decoder. Its prescribed code length entails that the assigned numerical code fit within that many bits. The assigned fits_in_bits contract supplies this width predicate through canonical_range_fits during construction. This is a local representation/width contribution to B.3, not a finding that the helper performs the complete histogram, recurrence, ordering, or unique-code algorithm. The nonempty count precondition belongs to the caller canonical_range_fits and is guarded by construction; unused PREFLEN=0 lines are not treated as zero-width active codes.

Annex B explicitly forms an integral part of the standard, so the imperative B.3/B.4 algorithms are applicable despite lacking modal keywords. B.4's extracted MAY sentence about numeric/OOB results is not the prefix-match requirement; the full-text passage is therefore the right evidence ID. Other lexical MAY annotations include optional descriptive prose and even copyright text; no lexical annotation alone was treated as binding decoder behavior.

Source survey followed wide.rs into decoding.rs, construction.rs, HuffmanTable's private metadata and HuffmanLines adapters in src/huffman.rs, the project's specs/huffman.rs result/representation models, src/reader.rs bit ordering, and the adjacent validate_lines implementation. The actual production decode_fallback calls append_bit/small_distance_from even though prior stored graph summaries reported missing incoming edges; cfg(test) decode_canonical was distinguished and not used as execution evidence. canonical_range_fits is called only for nonzero buckets in the inspected construction loop. Ordered-line buckets preserve original line order. There is also a prefix-lookup path; these findings concern fallback arithmetic and construction support, not its complete equivalence. docs/spec-traceability.md expressly distinguishes partial functional project contracts, source hashes and independent standard fidelity; config/support-matrix.json names the T.88 (08/2018)/ISO 14492:2019 decoder baseline, standard/custom Huffman support, and distinct T.6 MMR support.

T.6 changing-element/MMR procedures, raster/template/rendering operations, page composition, segment lengths/retention, extension comments, colour palette input, informative Annex J encoder components, and Annex H examples do not independently impose requirements on these four helpers. T.88 6.4.10 and 7.4.3.1.7 are potential broader symbol-ID callers of B.3-style codes, but their complete endpoint wiring was not audited. No low score, unrelated candidate, or empty retrieval was converted to a not_implemented finding.

document_quote.quote: This is a four-byte value containing the width in pixels of the page's bitmap.

documentation_quotes.quote:
"policy": "Defaults are independently configurable downward. Raising a limit requires an explicit Limits value and remains subject to checked arithmetic and platform representability.",
    "max_width": 1000000,

Project resource limits and typed Rust error policy are separate from normative
rules. A policy row does not increase the standard-requirement count.

findings.rationale: This is a documented restriction of the default acceptance domain relative to the four-byte width representation, not a change to that representation. Limits::project_default sets max_width to 1,000,000; Limits::default delegates to it; Decoder::project_default passes that policy to Decoder::new. The inspected page parser reads a u32 width and checks the cap, returning LimitExceeded with LimitKind::Width rather than truncating the width. The known-height branch uses enforce_dimension_limits; the unknown-height branch separately checks width. Thus the restriction is intentional project resource policy, not an unexplained parser-field-width defect. The disposition does not assert that 7.4.8.1 obliges an implementation to allocate every representable page, nor that finite limits alone violate normative conformance. The adjacent 7.4.8.2 unknown-height sentinel was inspected and must not be mistaken for an ordinary height exceeding the cap. This mapping covers initialization and the inspected consumer path only, not universal dimension-limit enforcement or whole-decoder compliance.
findings.relevance: T.88 (08/2018) 7.4.8.1 defines the page-width field consumed by this library in its decoder role. Both assigned contracts initialize max_width to 1,000,000. The connection applies when Decoder is constructed with these defaults and encounters a page information segment, in standalone or embedded segment processing. It does not concern an encoder or a fax-terminal negotiation endpoint. Assume an otherwise applicable, well-formed bi-level stream; other policy limits and unsupported features remain independent.

code_quotes.quote: max_references_per_segment: 4_096,

document_quote.quote: Bits 0-28       Count of referred-to segments. This specifies the number of segments that this segment refers to.

documentation_quotes.quote:
/// Maximum references declared by one segment.
    pub max_references_per_segment: u32,
"policy": "Defaults are independently configurable downward. Raising a limit requires an explicit Limits value and remains subject to checked arithmetic and platform representability."
"max_references_per_segment": 4096,
Segment, page, symbol, reference, and per-segment reference counts are bounded.

findings.rationale: The standard allocates 29 bits to the long-form count, whereas the assigned constructors deliberately choose a much smaller operational cap. parse_referred_segments first validates and extracts the long-form count, then enforces the configured reference limit before reading retention bytes and allocating the reference vector; it also enforces the limit for the short form. enforce_reference_limit rejects count > max_references_per_segment with a typed ReferencesPerSegment limit error. The source distinguishes the numeric-format rule from this project quota: validate_long_count masks 0x1FFF_FFFF and rejects noncanonical short counts, while the separate quota uses Limits. The full 7.2.4 section, including forbidden count codes 5/6 and retention-bit semantics, was read; 7.4.2.2 also confirms that symbol dictionary decoding consumes arrays from referred dictionaries. No finding about retention correctness or decoding all referenced dictionaries is inferred from the constructor. This disposition records a documented acceptance restriction relative to the format's count domain, not a claim that the standard mandates allocating the maximum count or that a resource-policy rejection is inherently a conformance defect.
findings.relevance: T.88 (08/2018) 7.2.4 defines the per-segment long-form reference count. Both assigned default-policy contracts initialize max_references_per_segment to 4,096. This is relevant to the library as a decoder parsing segment headers, including standalone and embedded inputs using that policy. Assume an otherwise valid long-form field and semantically permitted references to available earlier segments; a numerically encodable count alone does not establish a valid document.

limitations: Partial standards alignment only. Both assigned specs were read in full, but only their width and per-segment-reference defaults received findings. No complete standard counterpart or absence argument was established for max_height, max_pixels_per_page, max_decoder_managed_memory_bytes, max_stream_bytes, max_pages, max_segments, max_symbols, max_total_references, max_reference_graph_depth, max_nesting_depth, max_work_units, max_cumulative_decoded_bitmap_bytes or max_retained_state_bytes; nearby height/page-count context is survey evidence only.

The assigned constructor frame guarantees are local project contracts, not separately mapped external-standard obligations.

T.88 7.4.8.2 reserves 0xFFFFFFFF for unknown height, and the parser recognizes it before enforcing known-height dimensions. They distinguish trusted caller resource policy, format rules and incomplete normative/resource-proof coverage. The two intentional_deviation dispositions mean documented bounded acceptance policies relative to wider format numeric domains, not assertions of normative nonconformance or defects.

result.notes: Standalone publication-only survey. get_work_item reported no prior-attempt feedback. Read the assigned contracts through read_specs, including full behavioral clauses, assumptions and entry conditions, and inspected the production MMR module, codes, memory, raster, reference, spans, termination and tables, plus shared reader/bitmap implementations and relevant generic-region, halftone and collective-symbol callers. Candidate retrieval was initiated for all 66 assigned Core specs; local retrieval artifacts contain a matching full-contract query for every assigned spec. Paginated one forward query and independently enumerated all 392 full-text passages and all 421 lexical obligations. Used reverse passage retrieval for T.88 6.2.6 and T.6 2.2.5.2. Retrieval is budgeted candidate discovery, not exhaustive relevance or conformance evidence. Direct concept searches for MMR, reference, pad bits and malformed-stream discretion supplied context missed or diluted by similarity. Corpus is fulltext+obligations/1, not legacy lexical-only. The document identities are T.6 (1988), text digest ce107ab4f36fb3b7a1f17f2e076472370144973b0e0e2202183ca994735d17e8, and T.88 (08/2018), digest 0caacf3891e7b059ef8090ec96029768b2621aa366ce4b37a3a56f743ec475c6. The latter conversion displays ISO/IEC 14492:2019 page furniture; no later T.88 edition is claimed. Section labels sometimes reflect page furniture: T.6 Tables 2 and 3 occur around anchors labeled 4 and 6; figures lose graphical content. Modal matching is case-insensitive lexical annotation, not a normative eligibility test: T.6 2.2.1, definitions, Table 1, algorithms and EOFB format are meaningful without MUST. Conversely copyright, patents, cross-reference advice, informative examples and lexical 'may' embedded in optional descriptions are not automatically implementation requirements. T.88 6.1 says behavior on bitstreams violating restrictions is undefined; typed errors, rollback priority and fail-closed handling are project choices. docs/spec-traceability.md explicitly separates resource limits and typed Rust errors from normative rules and warns that project contracts do not establish independent standard fidelity. Relevant project policies include inclusive stream/work/memory limits, transition capacity accounting, logical clear versus allocation release, finite mode/run budgets and Rust ownership. These were surveyed in source but are not promoted to invented external requirements or defects. Optional EOFB no-check behavior is consistent with the approach described in T.88 6.2.6 Note 2 when the enclosing caller skips the known block; an unchanged internal reader is not by itself a byte-consumption violation. PatternMmr is single-use/Optional; GrayMmr is prefix-based/Required and advances by consumed bytes; the collective-symbol caller bounds source by BMSIZE and advances the outer bit reader over that block. Candidate matches for arithmetic BYTEIN/BYTEOUT/FLUSH, IAID, canonical Huffman prefix assignment, arithmetic generic/refinement context edges, page composition, text matching, comment encodings, profile stripes and patent text are unrelated to the assigned MMR helper obligations unless a separately inspected caller establishes relevance. In particular arithmetic encoder termination is not an MMR EOFB rule, and document extension segments are not T.6 extension mode codes. No out_of_scope findings or missing-implementation conclusions were created from those candidates. The T.6 make-up selection procedure is an encoding rule; decoder acceptance of other bounded make-up sequences was not treated as a defect. Review-marked Core reference facts were used normally with ordered-cache and skipped-prefix assumptions. result.notes:
Standalone, source-only publication survey of the 37 assigned Core specs on 21 src/segment_header.rs components. get_work_item and rfc_inventory were read. Every assigned subject's complete contracts were requested with read_specs; large responses were read in bounded ranges. Every assigned spec received a successful forward retrieve_document_candidates_for_spec call; the first parallel batch intermittently returned unknown-work-item errors, so affected calls were retried individually. SOMA is local and budgeted, never an eligibility threshold. Forward budgets varied (500, 1000, 1200, 1500, 5000 or 8000 tokens), so candidate totals are budget-relative, not corpus sizes. Pagination was exercised for reference_width (offsets 0 and 5), search_rfc('segment header') (offsets 0 and 10), full-text enumeration (0..2 and 170..184 of 392 passages), and lexical enumeration (0..2 and 148..199 of 421 annotations). Search additionally used 'referred-to segment count' and 'All other segment types'; 'most significant byte' returned no text hits and was not interpreted as absence. Reverse retrieval was performed from passages 7.2.4, 7.2.5, 7.2.6, 7.2.7 and 7.3 and the reserved-count obligation. Results sometimes ranked unrelated scalar/bitmap algorithms or reference-limit specs highly; final associations instead follow the actual contracts, standard sections and source.

Read full local T.88 sections 7.2.1 through 7.2.8 and 7.3, plus retrieved 7.1 context. The source edition is ITU-T T.88 (08/2018), PDF-converted text displaying ISO/IEC 14492:2019 (E), sha256 0caacf3891e7b059ef8090ec96029768b2621aa366ce4b37a3a56f743ec475c6. The other assigned document is T.6 (1988 Blue Book extract), sha256 ce107ab4f36fb3b7a1f17f2e076472370144973b0e0e2202183ca994735d17e8; its facsimile code tables and MMR coding are not segment-header requirements. T.88 6.2.6 cross-reference/exception material may govern the MMR decoder, not these count and field helpers. No older-edition evidence is claimed to establish a later edition's conformance.

Reusable survey facts: retention is wire-byte order and LSB-first within a byte; index zero is the current segment, and reference i uses index i+1. Short unused bits are distinct from count bits; long padding is in the final wire byte. Current segment numbers 256 and 65536 are inclusive width boundaries. Canonical long counts exceed four and occupy the low 29 bits. Numeric backward-reference validation is separate from target existence/type/page validation. parse_segment_header is header-only: sequential callers then read payload, whereas random-access callers first collect headers. Unknown length is represented as None only for type 38, and read_payload selects the generic marker scanner. Nonempty accessor and reader-position premises from review-marked Core facts were retained, not discarded because of needs_review labels.

Important document ambiguity: T.88 7.2.8 example 2 presents retention bytes '02 FD' for nine references and says the current segment is retained. Read literally in 7.2.4 wire order, the first byte's bit zero is false and the final byte has nonzero unused bits; the explicit field definition instead supports 'FD 02' for the stated decisions. src/segment_header/tests.rs:parses_long_form_header documents this with the exact source comment '// The worked example conflicts with 7.2.4; follow the explicit field rules.' and checks rejection before swapping bytes. This is retained as a survey note about an informative example, not a normative implementation defect or a fabricated out-of-scope finding. No test was executed.

Source followed beyond the assignment into src/reader.rs, src/document/parsing.rs, src/document/references.rs, src/decode/resources.rs, src/limits.rs, specs/segments.rs and README.md. Project-authored ghost annotations/models provide documented local intent, not independent normative authority or proof results. Limits are explicit inclusive caller policy; the default reference cap is 4096, with a long-form cap check before retention reads/allocation and short-form retention construction before the common check. These policy, allocation, ownership and diagnostic details are not automatically requirements of T.88. README explicitly disclaims full JBIG2/Annex F compliance and excludes encoding and colour decoding. Unrelated SOMA candidates (T.6 terminating/make-up tables; T.88 arithmetic coding Annexes A/E/H; bitmap/refinement algorithms 6.x; extension payload syntax 7.4.14) were not converted to findings merely on similarity. Optional bit-7 optimization in the 7.2.3 NOTE is not a mandatory optimization requirement.

No inference, build, tests, proofs, protocol/model execution, legacy pipeline, source changes or external-network research were performed. Quotations are file/section evidence, not host-verified function attributions or semantic proofs. Stored alignment is restricted to the quoted requirements and assumptions, not whole-component or whole-document compliance.

result.notes:
Standalone publication pass; no inference, tests, proofs, or legacy pipeline were run. Read get_work_item (no previous attempts/review notes) and rfc_inventory, then read_specs and the full natural-language contracts, assumptions, requires/formal clauses for all 84 assigned specs across 40 component subjects. Corpus is fulltext+obligations/1, not lexical-only. Enumerated all 392 full-text passages with offsets 0,5,105,205,305 and all 421 lexical obligations with offsets 0,5,105,205,305,405; enumeration is not a claim that every passage was investigated. Used spec-first SOMA for selected contracts, paginated packed-bitmap candidates (offsets 0 and 5), reverse passage retrieval for 6.5.9 and A.1, and reverse obligation retrieval for the 6.4.11 byte-count requirement. These results were candidate leads only. Concept searches included collective bitmap, IARDW, 0xFF, and 6.5.8.2.4; original sections were read around geometry, header sequencing, dictionary array order, IAID, context isolation, reset state, marker rules and minimization.

Reusable source survey: src/symbol_text/bitmap.rs handles packed collective bitmap storage, template mapping, cropping and fallible deep copying. dictionary/huffman.rs selects uncompressed versus MMR data from BMSIZE, aligns before bounded fields, and splits collective bitmaps using accumulated widths. codebook.rs implements ordered imported-plus-decoded-new lookup; its reference identity/ownership contracts are project API choices, not independent ITU requirements. codec/arithmetic.rs retains a common arithmetic stream with separate integer/IAID/refinement banks. codec/huffman.rs distinguishes prepared text-region symbol-ID tables from fixed-width dictionary IDs; each Huffman refinement creates a local arithmetic decoder while retaining refinement statistics. codec/refinement.rs constructs text-instance geometry using floor, not truncation, and must not be substituted for dictionary/arithmetic.rs's fixed-size single-instance procedure. Generic/refinement kernels, bitmap storage/access/composition, arithmetic integer decoding, preparation macros and text callers were inspected beyond assigned helpers.

Unrelated/insufficient candidates retained only here: T.6 preamble copyright wording and Group 4 terminal negotiation, Teletex/mixed-mode, greyscale/colour material do not impose these helper contracts. Lexical modality extraction can mislabel ordinary text (including Optional/bitmap contexts); MUST/SHOULD/MAY labels were not treated as eligibility or normative verdicts. SOMA also returned T.88 encoder BYTEOUT/probability-estimation sections, file-organization D.3, generic segment row-count handling, halftone material and Annex H examples: these do not automatically apply to assigned symbol helper behavior. T.88 5.6's black/white interpretation is explicitly an application convention, not a mandatory pixel-value interpretation. The README documents black=1/MSB-first representation and explicitly disclaims full JBIG2/Annex F profile conformance. Generic template helper fallback for arbitrary bytes >=4 and refinement fallback for bytes >1 are not wire-format defects: dictionary header extraction bounds these fields to two and one bits respectively. Error-preserving conversion, local memory/work accounting and Rust ownership guarantees are useful Core contracts but were not manufactured into external normative requirements. Source quotes and existing review-marked summaries are source-supported assessments with their assumptions, not host-verified function attributions or semantic proofs. Stored alignment here is not whole-component or whole-standard compliance.
